The present application under Section 430 read with Section 528 of the BNSS has been filed seeking suspension of sentence and release of the applicant/appellant on bail during pendency of the instant appeal.

3. Vide the impugned judgment of conviction and order on sentence dated 26.02.2024 and 23.04.2024 respectively, the appellant has been convicted for the offences punishable under Sections 304B/498A of the IPC.

The appellant has been sentenced to undergo 10 years of rigorous imprisonment for offence punishable under Section 304B of the IPC alongwith fine of Rs. 50,000/-
and rigorous imprisonment for 2 years for offence punishable under Section 498A of the IPC alongwith fine of Rs. 20,000/-.
4.
Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the appellant/applicant submits that the latter was put to trial alongwith his father-Parmal Singh, mother- This is a digitally signed order.

It is pointed out that vide the impugned judgment, the learned Trial Court after detailed analysis came to the finding that the ingredients of Section 304B of the IPC with respect to the words, "soon before death" could not be Dev Pal @ Pappu vs State (Nct Of Delhi) on 4 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129960793/
1 made with respect to other co-accused persons and also that the prosecution had failed to establish the charge for offence punishable under Section 498A of the IPC against the said co-accused persons.
5. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the appellant/applicant draws attention of this Court to the statement (Ex.PW-1/B) made by father of the deceased before the SDM to demonstrate that there was no demand for dowry soon before the death even qua the present appellant/applicant.
Attention of this Court is also drawn to the statement of PW-17 who was cited by the prosecution claiming to be the mediator, who in his testimony before the learned Trial Court has clearly stated that there is no demand of dowry by the appellant as well as his family members.

sentences.text: It is further submitted that the appellant has two daughters who are living with his parents, and therefore, his presence is required to look after them.

It is further submitted that the appellant was on bail during the pendency of the trial before the learned Trial Court and nothing has come on record to show that he had misused the liberty granted to him.
It is further submitted that even during the pendency of the captioned appeal, the appellant was released on interim bail and he had duly surrendered after expiry of the same.

6. Per contra, learned APP for the State submits that the post-mortem report shows there were ante-mortem injuries on the body of the deceased and the learned Trial Court on the basis of the aforesaid injuries had come to the conclusion that the deceased was subject to cruelty soon before her death.
It This is a digitally signed order.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 04/03/2025 at 22:22:54 is further submitted that the said injuries could not be explained by the present appellant during the course of the trial, and thus, the conviction is to be sustained.

7. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
8.

Learned Trial Court while convicting the present appellant has observed that PWs-1, 2, 3 and 4, in their testimonies, had stated that one week prior to the date of the incident, the deceased has come to the house and at that time on the insistence of the present appellant a sum of Rs. 50,000/- and one gold chain was sent through the brother of the deceased.
It is pertinent to note that the aforesaid allegation was missing from the initial complaint made by PW-1 and was accordingly confronted with his previous statement.

Relevant portion of the testimony of PW-1 before the learned Trial Court reads as under: -
"It is correct that I had not stated to SDM in my statement that my son Sony took Kavita to her matrimonial house.
He also took Rs. 50,000/- in cash and a gold chain for accused persons.
I had given money and gold chain to my son as accused Dev Pal had demanded the same for his business."

9. It is pertinent to note that learned Trial Court has disbelieved the allegations of demand of dowry soon before death qua the other family members of the present appellant but came to the conclusion Dev Pal @ Pappu vs State (Nct Of Delhi) on 4 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129960793/
2 with regard to the same qua the present appellant on the basis of the aforesaid statement.

sentences.text: 10. The appellant was on bail during the pendency of the trial before the learned Trial Court.
Nominal roll dated 04.12.2024 shows that the appellant has undergone incarceration for approximately 2 years and 10 months.
11. In totality of the facts and circumstances of the case, the sentence awarded to applicant/appellant, is suspended and he is directed to be released
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 04/03/2025 at 22:22:55 on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs. 50,000/- with one surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the Trial Court/Link Court, further subject to the following conditions:
-
i.
The applicant/appellant shall not leave the country without prior permission of this Court.

ii. The applicant/appellant shall intimate this Court by way of an affidavit and to the Investigating Officer regarding any change in residential address.
iii.
The applicant/appellant shall appear before this Court as and when the matter is taken up for hearing.
iv. The applicant/appellant shall provide his mobile number to the Investigating Officer and intimate about any change.
12. In view of the aforesaid, the application is allowed and disposed of accordingly.

13. Needless to state that, nothing stated hereinabove, is an opinion on the merits of the present appeal and any observations made herein are only for the purpose of the present application.
14. Copy of the order be sent to the concerned Jail Superintendent for necessary information and compliance.
15. Order be uploaded on the website of this Court forthwith.
16. List in due course.
